pages.name: Lost
pages.blurb: Steve Bicknell and Sheree Rashit's warehouse night; Jeff Mills's London home.

pages.name: fabric
pages.blurb: Three rooms under Smithfield; the bodysonic floor; closed September 2016, reopened January 2017.

pages.name: Berghain / Panorama Bar
pages.blurb: A 1953 power plant, with Panorama Bar from October 2004 and the main floor from December; Funktion-One and Klubnacht.

pages.name: Tresor
pages.blurb: The Wertheim vault from 13 March 1991 to 2005; the Kraftwerk power station from 2007.

pages.name: Space
pages.blurb: Playa d'en Bossa, the Terrace under the flight path; Carl Cox 2001–16; ENTER.; closed 2 October 2016.

pages.name: Castlemorton Common, May 1992
pages.blurb: A week-long free festival of 20–40,000 on a Worcestershire common; the end of the free party era and the beginning of acid techno's exile.

pages.name: Roland TR-909
pages.blurb: Drum machine — Roland's first with MIDI; the kick, hats and clap of house and techno for forty years.

pages.name: Detroit
pages.blurb: Motor City. Techno's birthplace: Belleville, the Music Institute, UR, Submerge, Movement.

pages.name: The Haçienda
pages.blurb: FAC 51; empty for years, then Nude (1986) and Hot (1988) made it Britain's first house club; closed by guns and debt.

pages.name: Trade
pages.blurb: Turnmills, Sunday mornings; Tony De Vit; the gay after-hours that became hard house.

pages.name: Glastonbury Festival
pages.blurb: The festival at Worthy Farm, where dance music moved from market stalls and travellers' fields to the Pyramid Stage between 1989 and 1997.

pages.name: Sabresonic
pages.blurb: Andrew Weatherall's Friday techno night at Happy Jax under London Bridge, where the Chemical Brothers played their first live gig.
